subject: science

concepts.title: Classification of Mixtures
concepts.definition: Mixtures are categorized using the uniformity of their composition into homogeneous and heterogeneous types.
concepts.key_idea: Homogeneous mixtures have uniform distribution, while heterogeneous mixtures have visible boundaries.
question_patterns: classify the following as homogeneous or heterogeneous
is a mixture of oil and water homogeneous
give examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures
how can we distinguish between a solution and a suspension

solution_steps.explain: Check if the components are spread evenly and if there are visible boundaries between them.
If particles are visible to the naked eye or settle over time, it is heterogeneous.

concepts.title: Mass by Mass Percentage
concepts.definition: A method to express concentration by calculating the mass of solute relative to the total mass of the solution.
concepts.key_idea: Concentration based on the weight of components.
question_patterns: calculate the mass by mass percentage of the solution
find the concentration of salt in water by mass
what is the percentage concentration if ...g is dissolved in ...g
determine the mass percentage of a solute

solution_steps.explain: Add the mass of the solute and the mass of the solvent to get the total solution mass.
Divide the solute mass by the total solution mass and multiply by 100.

concepts.title: Mass by Volume Percentage
concepts.definition: Concentration expressed as the mass of solute present in 100 units of volume of the solution.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Commonly used for liquid both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both medicines and laboratory reagents.
question_patterns: find the mass by volume percentage
calculate the concentration in % m/v
how much solute is in 100mL of a ...% solution
calculate the concentration of glucose in saline

solution_steps.explain: Take the mass of the solute and divide it by the total volume of the solution.
Multiply the ratio by 100 to get the percentage concentration.

concepts.title: Solubility and Saturated Solutions
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, Solubility is indeed the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a specific amount of solvent at a fixed temperature.
concepts.key_idea: Saturated solutions cannot dissolve more solute at a given temperature.
question_patterns: what mass of salt is needed to make a saturated solution
calculate the solubility of ... at ... degrees
how much solute will precipitate on cooling
find the amount of solute required for ...g of water

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the standard solubility (per 100g) by the given solvent mass and divide by 100.

concepts.title: Crystallization
concepts.definition: A purification technique where a pure solid is separated from a solution by forming crystals as the solvent cools or evaporates.
concepts.key_idea: Based on the decrease in solubility of solids with decreasing temperature.
question_patterns: how are pure crystals of copper sulfate obtained
explain the process of crystallization
why is crystallization better than simple evaporation
how to separate a pure solid from an impure sample

solution_steps.explain: Dissolve the substance in a minimum amount of hot solvent.
Remove insoluble impurities while hot, then allow the filtrate to cool slowly to form crystals.

concepts.title: Distillation
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, a process used to separate miscible liquids or a liquid from a solid by boiling the mixture and condensing the resulting vapors.
concepts.key_idea: Separates components using significant differences in boiling points.
question_patterns: how to separate acetone and water
explain the principle of distillation
when is distillation used for separation
how can we recover both solute and solvent from a solution

solution_steps.explain: Heat the liquid mixture in a flask until the component with the lower boiling point vaporizes.
Pass the vapors through a condenser cooled by water to turn them back into liquid form.

concepts.title: Paper Chromatography
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, a technique used to separate constituents of a mixture, like dyes in ink, using their different rates of movement through a medium.
concepts.key_idea: Separation depends on solubility and interaction with the stationary phase.
question_patterns: how to separate pigments in black ink
what is the principle of chromatography
can we separate colors in a flower petal
explain the use of chromatography in forensic science

solution_steps.explain: Place a small drop of the mixture on a strip of filter paper.
Dip the end of the paper in a solvent so it rises, carrying components at different speeds.

concepts.title: Separating Funnel
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, a device used to separate two immiscible liquids that form distinct layers using their densities.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Heavier liquid settles at the both bottom and is drained first.
question_patterns: how to separate oil and water
explain the use of a separating funnel
which layer will be at the bottom in an oil-water mixture
how to separate two immiscible liquids

solution_steps.explain: Pour the mixture into the funnel and let it stand until two clear layers appear.
Open the stopcock to collect the denser liquid from the bottom into a separate container.

concepts.title: Sublimation
concepts.definition: In brief, the direct transition of a material from solid to gas phase upon heating, used to separate sublimable solids from non-sublimable ones.
concepts.key_idea: Separates substances like camphor or naphthalene from sand or salt.
question_patterns: how to separate camphor and sand
define sublimation with examples
how to separate naphthalene from common salt
what happens when dry ice is heated

solution_steps.explain: Gently heat the mixture in a dish covered with an inverted funnel.
The sublimable substance vaporizes and deposits as a solid on the cool inner walls of the funnel.

concepts.title: Centrifugation
concepts.definition: A method that uses rapid rotation to force denser particles to the bottom of a container, separating them from the liquid.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Used for separating cream from milk or blood cells from plasma.
question_patterns: how is cream separated from milk
explain the principle of centrifugation
how are blood components separated in a lab
what is a paperfuge

solution_steps.explain: Rotate the mixture at high speed in a centrifuge machine.
The heavier particles move to the bottom while the lighter liquid stays on top.

concepts.title: Tyndall Effect
concepts.definition: The phenomenon where light is scattered by particles in a colloid or suspension, making the beam's path visible.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Distinguishes true solutions from both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both colloids and suspensions.
question_patterns: why is the path of light visible in milk but not in salt water
define the Tyndall effect
give examples of Tyndall effect in daily life
how to identify a colloid using a laser

solution_steps.explain: Direct a narrow beam of light through the liquid mixture.
If the path of light is visible from the side, the mixture is a colloid or suspension.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If {mass_solute} g of salt is dissolved in {mass_solvent} g of water, calculate the mass by mass percentage of the solution formed.

solution_template.explain: Sum of solute and solvent mass.
Solute mass divided by solution mass times 100.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If {mass_solute} g of glucose is dissolved in water to make {volume_solution} mL of solution, calculate its concentration in mass by volume percentage.

solution_template.explain: Mass of solute divided by volume of solution times 100.
